1. The animation shows a mortgage as a grid of payment blocks, and it compares two ways of paying. One is the usual monthly payment of $732.67. The other is the same amount paid as one lump sum of $8,792 a year (12 × $732.67). Tessa is an illustrative character standing next to a house.

2. At first the grid is full of blocks. The blocks then get used up and turn dark, as payments knock the loan down. In the last frames the camera zooms in on the grid. Most of it is dark, a few blocks are still lit at the top, and a gold block group appears at the end. The caption then changes to "ends in 184 months: 4 months later than monthly."

3. Paying the same total once a year instead of monthly is slightly worse. The loan takes 184 months to pay off instead of 180, which is 4 months longer. This is because interest accrues in the meantime and the money goes in later. The gold blocks at the end are the extra 4 months.

4. The only takeaway a viewer would get is narrow. Spreading payments out monthly beats saving up and paying once a year, at the same total amount. The animation says nothing on whether to pay extra or invest the spare cash. It gives no advice on that question, and no rates of return are shown.

5. The animation itself suggested the narrow takeaway, through its on-screen text: "ends in 184 months: 4 months later than monthly." Its labels say "ILLUSTRATIVE" and "US only · history, not a forecast," which tell the viewer not to treat it as a prediction or as personal advice. The pay-extra-versus-invest question is my own context and is not in the animation, and I am not drawing any conclusion about it from this image.
